title: Photon-Induced Near Fields of Oxide-Modified Aluminum Nanoparticles
content: Plasmonic nanoparticles exhibit greatly enhanced electric fields near their surface upon photoexcitation, enabling applications in sensing, catalysis, and energy conversion [1]. In this study, we employ photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) [2] within an ultrafast electron microscope to investigate the polarization and power-dependent plasmonic responses produced by individual oxide-modified aluminum nanocrystals. By leveraging PINEM’s spatial resolution, we aimed to enhance our understanding of how modifying a nanostructure impacts localized surface plasmon resonances by providing nanoscale insight into optical near fields to better understand and predict behavior in applications.
